scope: 51 individually listed stranded members; three archive verdicts preserved
context: Kali/Empire/DAVtest provenance makes authorized security testing plausible. Each listed member is a functional attack payload/module rather than documentation or an inert vendored library. Individual malicious verdicts follow credential harvesting, surveillance, exploitation or remote-control implementation, including the working test-directory Mimikatz. This does not prove unauthorized deployment. No operator authorization, victim configuration, runtime success or final remote payload is inferred. The macOS installer additionally has a configured collection endpoint and deceptive password/replacement/persistence paths.
method: Fresh atomscan scans and cleave facts for all 51 members; source execution paths, Base64/Gzip/Deflate reconstruction, CLR IL and native disassembly; no sample execution. Baseline uses a git HEAD rules snapshot, final uses this checkout. Both comparison scans use --follow=none.
count_method: Unique trait IDs over each original file and its decoded/extracted stages. Fetched URL/dependency entries and fetch verdicts are excluded. Archive counts select the requested archive and its own member tree. Per-file calibrated ML results are retained.

changes.change: Admit Mach-O carriers of decoded AppleScript; preserve the matcher, severity, and original script scopes.
changes.evidence: ARM64 main at 0x100000690 obtains decoded text and calls system at 0x1000006b8. XOR uses seed 0x11667, multiplier 0x3785 and modulus 35999 derived from embedded 09:59:59. Independently reconstructed 445-line AppleScript matches recovered facts, including the masked Installation dialog and dscl authonly retry loop.
changes.consumer_audit: Existing consumers retain script-only scopes, so the Mach-O expansion does not broaden their coverage or suppression.

controls: check.py: positive validated dialog and actual original Mach-O; password-only, directory-authentication-only and PDF-password near misses rejected. Existing script positive retained.

members.marker_note: Mac Installer: steals secrets and persists; fix native phish scope
members.evidence: ARM64 main calls the PRNG/XOR decoder then system() with its decoded osascript command. The recovered AppleScript validates a fake Installation password prompt with dscl, copies browser/keychain/wallet/Notes/documents into a random /tmp directory, zips and curl-posts it to the configured host, deletes staging, replaces Ledger Live and bootstraps a system LaunchDaemon. These paths are attempted even though remote payload bytes and runtime success are unknown.

members.evidence: MainAgent.process_packet dispatches network task types to compile/exec, subprocess shells, uploads/downloads and jobs. file_download reads local chunks, encodes them and builds type-41 response packets. run() consumes packet-handler tasking.
members.classifier_disagreement: Functional attack payload has supported hostile findings, but the calibrated classifier does not alert; no severity inflation was used.

members.marker_note: Empire C stager: downloads raw code and executes it as a fiber

remaining_detection_limitations: Single-purpose payloads below three hostile traits have specific coverage_goal_limit entries. Native API presence is not promoted into unproven independent theft, persistence or C2. Generic reflected loading and local file output remain capabilities. Unknown remote payloads, runtime success and authorization are not inferred.
validation: Run make validate as the final action after this report and markers are written.
engine_variation: The universal Mach-O member inside the archive selected an x64 XOR observation in the baseline and an ARM64 XOR observation in the final scan. Both slices contain and decode the same AppleScript. The independently scanned member selected the same slice in both runs and lost no trait. Neither XOR matcher was edited; archive hostile/suspicious counts lost nothing.
classifier_limit: The installed model is v18.18 (feature spec 18); the engine warns that its current feature spec is 21. Twenty-six malicious payload members have calibrated FP level -1 in both comparable runs despite supported hostile traits. This is reported as a classifier gap, not repaired by duplicate or inaccurate traits.
